newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian call money firms on liquidity squeeze.
newsitem.headline: Croatian call money firms on liquidity squeeze.

text.p: The Croatian call money rates firmed to between 9.0 and 12 percent from 9.0 percent in the morning trade on a Friday liquidity squeeze, dealers said.
"Demand tops very short supply by banks due to the (end-of-week) tax payment," one dealer told Reuters.
She said rates went up as banks ran short and funds from other lenders, including the bourse, insurers and money market, is subject to a mandatory reserve payment that tops 35 percent.
Interbank call money remained stable at 9.0 percent and one-month loans were struck at 11 percent.
But some borrowers were seen as resorting for help to the central bank through its Lombard facility before trading was over. Lombard loans are granted at 11 percent.
Thursday's overnight trade totalled 26 million kuna, used to cover the shortfalls and maintain reserves at three banks. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
